snp3.2:1.1:
To me—
my mind resolute in exertion
snp3.2:1.3:
making a great effort,
doing jhāna
snp3.2:1.4: to attain rest from the yoke—
snp3.2:3.1:
Death
has 1,000 parts of you.
Only one part
snp3.2:3.3:
Live, good sir!
Life is better.
snp3.2:3.4:
Alive,
you can do
acts of merit.
snp3.2:4.4: What use is exertion to you?
snp3.2:5.1:
Hard to follow
—the path of exertion—
snp3.2:5.2:
hard to do, hard
to sustain.”
snp3.2:5.4: Māra stood in the Awakened One’s presence.
snp3.2:6.1: And to that Māra, speaking thus,
snp3.2:7.2:
for merit,
even the least bit of need.
snp3.2:7.3: Those who have need of merit:
snp3.2:7.4:
Those are the ones
Māra’s fit to address.
snp3.2:8.1:
In me are
conviction
austerity,
persistence,
snp3.2:8.3: Why, when my mind is resolute,
snp3.2:8.4:
do you petition me
to live?
snp3.2:9.1:
This wind could burn up
even river currents.
snp3.2:9.3: Why, when my mind is resolute,
snp3.2:11.3:
the mind has no interest
in sensuality.
snp3.2:12.1: Sensual passions are your first army.
snp3.2:15.3:
A coward can’t defeat it,
but one having defeated it
snp3.2:16.3: Death in battle would be better for me
snp3.2:17.1:
Sinking here, they don’t appear,
some brahmans & contemplatives.
snp3.2:17.4:
by which those with good practices
go.
snp3.2:18.3:
on all sides—
the troops, Māra
along with his mount—
I go into battle.
snp3.2:18.4:
May they not budge me
from
my spot.
snp3.2:19.2:
that the world with its devas
can’t overcome,
snp3.2:19.4: as an unfired pot with a stone.
snp3.2:20.3: I will go about, from kingdom to kingdom,
snp3.2:21.4:
where, having gone,
there’s no grief.”
snp3.2:23.3:
—’Maybe I’ve found
something tender here.
Maybe there’s something delicious’—
snp3.2:23.4: but not getting anything delicious there,
snp3.2:24.3: Like the crow attacking the rock,
snp3.2:25.1: As he was overcome with sorrow,
snp3.2:25.2: his lute fell from under his arm.
